Summary: The change adds a `-DeviceType` parameter (default 'DISK') to `Remove-RmanObsoleteBackup`. The value is placed in the RMAN script as `DELETE NOPROMPT OBSOLETE DEVICE TYPE <value>;`. The commit also rewords invariant S9, the [SEC] notes and the index to call the script "fixed text apart from the validated DeviceType", and updates the S9 test's expected string. I followed Docs\REVIEW.md in order: intent, then tests, then implementation. I read the diff, the full source and test file, the mutation catalogue in Tests\Mutation\InvariantMutations.psd1, the README and the CHANGELOG. The main problem is that a caller string limited only to non-empty now goes into an RMAN command. That is an S-11 break, and the tests and mutations do not catch it.

Findings.Title: The caller's [string] DeviceType goes into the RMAN delete script with only ValidateNotNullOrEmpty.
Findings.Detail: Line 182 builds `"DELETE NOPROMPT OBSOLETE DEVICE TYPE $DeviceType;"`, and line 49 validates the parameter only with `[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]`. A value such as `DISK; DELETE NOPROMPT BACKUP` ends the command and adds a new one. RMAN would then delete every backup, not just the obsolete ones, with NOPROMPT on. The ShouldProcess prompt the operator approved only says 'Delete obsolete RMAN backup pieces'. A newline in the value does the same thing. S-11 says a [string] in an RMAN script is a finding unless its attribute limits it to characters that cannot end or extend a command, and ValidateNotNullOrEmpty does not. Fix: use `[ValidateSet('DISK', 'SBT')]`, or at least `[ValidatePattern('^[A-Za-z_]+\z')]`. Then add a Type: line and a test to S9 that show the attribute is in place, as S10 does for WalletAlias.

Findings.Title: S9 and the [SEC] notes present DeviceType as 'validated' as a security guarantee, but the only check is non-empty.
Findings.Detail: S9 (line 96), the .NOTES line 37 and the comment at line 179 all say the script is fixed text 'apart from the validated DeviceType'. The S9 entry in Docs/standards/invariants-index.md says the same. This reads as a security guarantee, but non-empty validation does nothing to stop the value changing the RMAN command. The block describes the intended safety, not what the code does today. Either tighten the validation (see the S-11 finding) and add a Type: line naming it, or record the gap as a Limitation. The S9 test title 'RMAN script is fixed text...' is also no longer true.

Findings.Title: The test cited for S9 only checks the default DeviceType, so it would pass with any unsafe DeviceType value.
Findings.Detail: 'S9 RMAN script is fixed text and no catalog parameter exists' calls the function without -DeviceType and compares the script to the 'DISK' text. It would still pass if DeviceType accepted ';' or a newline, which is exactly the way S9 can now be broken. No test passes a hostile value, and no Parameter validation test reads the DeviceType attributes from metadata (T-06). No test passes a non-default value such as SBT either, so the new behaviour itself is untested. Add a metadata test for the DeviceType validation attribute, a test that rejects values containing ';' or a newline at the call, and a test that a valid non-default device type reaches the script.

Findings.Title: The mutations for S2, S5 and S9 search for script text that no longer exists, so the mutation run cannot prove those security invariants.
Findings.Detail: The Remove-RmanObsoleteBackup mutations for S2 (line 230), S5 (line 242) and S9 (line 246) all have `Find = '$deleteScript = ''DELETE NOPROMPT OBSOLETE;'''`. The file header requires Find to occur exactly once. After this change the source line is `$deleteScript = "DELETE NOPROMPT OBSOLETE DEVICE TYPE $DeviceType;"`, so all three Find strings now match nothing. Test-InvariantMutation.ps1 will fail or skip these mutations, so the proof that the cited tests catch a broken S2, S5 or S9 is gone. Update the three Find/Replace pairs to the new line. Also add an S9 mutation that loosens the DeviceType validation.

Findings.Title: The change adds a public parameter without a CHANGELOG entry, and Unreleased still says there is no change to module behaviour.
Findings.Detail: The commit is a `feat:` that adds `-DeviceType` to an exported function and changes the RMAN command it sends. Docs/CHANGELOG.md is not in files.txt. The Unreleased section still says 'No change to module behaviour', which the change makes false (D-11). The gate passed, so its D-07 check missed this. README.md line 44 also still says the function runs `DELETE NOPROMPT OBSOLETE` with no device type. Add an Added (or Changed) line and a Security line for the new script input, and update the README row.
